sources_considered.why: Readable primary disclosure of paid Copilot adoption and claimed customer benefits.
Independent survey evidence distinguishes product awareness and experimentation from frequent use.
Search found the announcement, but read_page could not retrieve it. The earnings-call source was used instead.
Search identified a contemporary technical-preview announcement, but read_page returned only an author biography. Its product claims cannot be quoted or used as outcome evidence.
The contemporary earnings call provides a clearer dated record for the observation window.

evidence_items.locator: Satya Nadella's prepared remarks, developers and GitHub Copilot
evidence_items.explanation: Microsoft reported current paid Copilot subscriptions of 1.8 million and identified customers seeing practical benefits. This makes coding assistance a serious counterexample candidate, but the disclosure does not establish retention, active use or independently verified gains.

evidence_items.publisher: Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism, University of Oxford
evidence_items.locator: Section 1, paragraph discussing Figure 3 and users aged 18–24
evidence_items.explanation: The six-country survey found limited frequency of ChatGPT use even among younger users. Fieldwork ended April 30 after beginning March 28; this supports caution about habitual consumer adoption, but cannot rule out a professional killer app.

unresolved_gaps: The records do not establish retention and sustained active use for the strongest professional candidate.
Consumer survey results cannot determine whether a specialist application qualifies.
The forthcoming-product search did not yield a readable primary announcement demonstrating compelling utility and likely sustained adoption.
No supplied threshold determines when useful, widely purchased software becomes a killer app.
